Lifecycle proof, not just help output

Write paths were validated with isolated disposable resources, a separate human approval for each mutation, and a read-only postcondition check.

Applications

Version and application lifecycle

Validated upload, read, version patch, version deletion, and direct parent deletion. Disposable applications were never assigned to a device.

Dispatch contract verified

CLI modernization delivered

The CLI now favors current APIs while retaining legacy commands only where no current replacement exists or behavior still requires the older contract.

01

Current APIs first

Superseded legacy command surfaces were removed through explicit path policy, not broad generation hiding.

02

Clear iOS naming

iOS-only resources use an explicit prefix while genuinely cross-platform commands remain neutral.

03

Platform-safe guidance

Generated agent guidance directs Linux, iOS, and Windows validation to current device APIs rather than Android compatibility routes.

04

Retired surfaces removed

v0 geofence and Foundry command surfaces were removed from the CLI while current v1 geofencing remains available.

Read-only coverage includes

  • Applications, versions, catalogs, and install status
  • Android, iOS, and Linux device queries using current APIs
  • Pipelines, runs, stages, targets, and command statistics
  • Policies, roles, scopes, reports, subscriptions, and content
  • Provisioning profiles, Apple app catalog, and DEP metadata
  • Telemetry, locations, events, heartbeats, and device state

Intentional boundaries and remaining prerequisites

  • Directory-record listing remains blocked by the onboarding feature flag; tenant Esper app listing returns HTTP 403 for this caller.
  • The AuthN user list still times out. Isolated configure tests and the script GET response-contract review have cleared their earlier blocked rows.
  • APNs certificate and provisioning creation require real integration artifacts.
  • Shared tenant and user mutations were not performed without a purpose-built disposable fixture.
  • Secure ADB and operational pipeline actions require dedicated runtime access and a separate action decision.
  • Non-Android devices were never deleted; platform checks used current device APIs only.
  • Known server-side alert-channel postcondition discrepancies are documented but were not investigated further.
  • An inactive disposable webtoken remains after an HTTP 200 delete response; its identifier and secret are excluded from this report.
OK

Evidence remains reviewable and sanitized.

The underlying local CSV preserves scenario outcomes, expected behavior, observed behavior, and prerequisites. This presentation intentionally excludes credentials, signed URLs, device identifiers, personal data, locations, certificate details, and raw API payloads.
